segments.line: Day one. School is cancelled. Probably.
Nobody can call anybody, so nobody knows. So nobody goes.
Your mom lights every candle in the house. Your
little sister Ellie digs an old board game out of the closet. You
play it by candlelight, and for the first time in years, nobody in your family looks at a phone. Ellie
wins three times. She cheats every time.
Day two. The freezer is melting. And the whole street has the same idea. Eat everything. Now. Neighbors you've never met drag their barbecues into the road. There's
steak for breakfast,
ice cream for lunch, and
fish fingers for absolutely nobody. Your
best friend Mo rides over on his bike. Bikes are suddenly the fastest thing in the city.
Every car is stuck exactly where it stopped, so kids ride down the middle of the highway where the traffic used to be. That
evening, Mo's dad builds a fire pit in his backyard and shows everyone how to cook rice in a pot over the flames. It
takes an hour. It's burnt.
Everybody eats it anyway. You and Mo ride to
the supermarket. The doors are wide open, and the manager is giving away melting ice cream for free, because it's better than throwing it away. You take
six tubs. And it's
quiet. Really quiet. No traffic. No hum. No buzz from the wires. You can hear birds in the middle of the city. At
night, people climb onto their roofs just to stare at the sky.
Light pollution hides the Milky Way from about eighty percent of North Americans. That's real.
Tonight, everyone sees it. Mo
lies next to you on the roof, eating the last ice cream in the neighborhood. 'Honestly, ' he says, 'this is kind of the best week ever. '
He's wrong. Because
tomorrow, the water stops.
